answer: Dynamic opportunity-cost bonds bind each identity to staking collateral C at rate r, so any Sybil replication incurs expected loss Δ=C·(e^{rT}-1) which the zephyr of marginal cost dominates. A subgame-perfect slashing matrix imposes penalty λC (λ>1) and a zero-knowledge verifiable delay forces disclosure before the gale of finality, yielding negative expected attack utility for all strategies. Consequently the strict Nash equilibrium rests on the frozen tundra of the protocol state where every agent stakes a single identity.
